aboutPage.title: About Us
aboutPage.body:
Sugeridor was built to solve a simple problem: tracking craft and specialty beer prices across several stores at once is tedious. We gather offers from different stores in one place, keep a price history for each product, and highlight when something is a genuinely good deal — so you don't miss a good offer or overpay out of impatience.

The catalog is updated periodically from partner stores. "View offer" links take you straight to the sale page on the store where the purchase actually happens — never here.

termsPage.title: Terms of Use
termsPage.body:
Sugeridor is a price-comparison and offer-aggregation site. We don't sell any product directly — every offer listed here belongs to and is sold by the store you're redirected to when clicking "View offer".

Prices shown reflect the last time we collected them and may have already changed at the store; always confirm the final price before completing a purchase. We're not responsible for price discrepancies, stock availability, or the sales policies of partner stores.

Some links may become affiliate links in the future — this will be disclosed when it happens.

stores.txtManualHint: For each field, give the START (text immediately before the value in the HTML) and the END (text immediately after). The TAG is optional and only matters on the first row: it is the marker that appears once per product (the card container). Leave it blank on the others. Name and Price are required.
stores.txtManualOrderWarning: Row order matters: the collector reads top to bottom and only moves forward through the HTML, never back. Put the fields in the same order they appear in the page source. The first row is the anchor that marks the start of each product.
stores.txtManualNeedsRequired: Fill in all three delimiters for Name and Price to be able to test.

stores.txtTagInsideIni: The tag for {fields} appears in the MIDDLE of the start text. That makes the collector skip to the next product and scramble the fields, with no error. Leave the tag blank on those rows (it falls back to the start text).

config.expirationHint: Offers not seen by the collector for more than this many days are automatically deactivated at the end of each run (price history is kept).
config.automationHint: Runs on its own at the end of every collection run (after enrichment), in the order text replacement → merge → slug resync. Requires the workflow secrets to be set up (SITE_BASE_URL/AUTOMATION_TOKEN on GitHub, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY/AUTOMATION_TOKEN on Vercel) — without them, nothing runs.
config.autoApplyReplacementsHint: Applies each active rule (one at a time, same order as the screen below) whenever the resulting slug doesn't collide with another product — never merges anything on its own.
config.autoMergeDuplicatesHint: Merges the by-name duplicates and the ones the active replacement rules would create, skipping pairs marked "ignore" in Tools. Resyncs slugs afterward (essential: otherwise the next collection duplicates the merged product).

config.thresholdHint: Triggers when the price drops by this much or more compared to the recent history average.

tools.hint: Actions that reprocess already-stored products. All are idempotent (running twice has no extra effect). Run on demand here, or turn it on in /admin/config to repeat automatically after every collection.
tools.applyAllHint: Runs every active find/replace rule in sequence, merges whatever duplicates are left, and resyncs identifiers — the same thing the post-collection automation does on its own (if enabled in /admin/config), just on demand. Use it after a manual collection instead of clicking rule by rule.
tools.applyAllResult: {rules, plural, =0 {No applicable rule.} =1 {1 rule applied,} other {# rules applied,}} {updated, plural, =0 {no product changed.} =1 {1 product changed.} other {# products changed.}} {merged, plural, =0 {} =1 {1 duplicate merged.} other {# duplicates merged.}} {resynced, plural, =0 {} =1 {1 identifier resynced.} other {# identifiers resynced.}} {conflicts, plural, =0 {No conflicts left.} =1 {1 conflict still needs your decision below.} other {# conflicts still need your decision below.}}
tools.actionsHint: Applied across the whole stored catalog.
tools.actionFailed: The action failed. Nothing was changed — please try again.
tools.normalizeResult: {count, plural, =0 {No name needed adjusting.} =1 {1 name adjusted.} other {# names adjusted.}} {conflicts, plural, =0 {} =1 {1 was skipped as a duplicate — resolve it by merging above.} other {# were skipped as duplicates — resolve them by merging above.}}
tools.reclassifyResult: {count, plural, =0 {No product changed category.} =1 {1 product reclassified.} other {# products reclassified.}}
tools.applyResult: {count, plural, =0 {No product changed} =1 {1 product changed} other {# products changed}}. {conflicts, plural, =0 {No conflicts.} =1 {1 conflict needs your decision below.} other {# conflicts need your decision below.}} {merged, plural, =0 {} =1 {1 duplicate merged automatically.} other {# duplicates merged automatically.}}
tools.rebrandResult: {count, plural, =0 {No brand needed adjusting} =1 {1 product rebranded} other {# products rebranded}}. {conflicts, plural, =0 {} =1 {1 case was skipped due to an identifier conflict.} other {# cases were skipped due to identifier conflicts.}}
tools.conflictsHint: These records would end up with the same identifier after the replacements, meaning they are the same product stored twice. Until they are merged, the rule affecting them has nothing safe to write. Merging moves the offers into a single product (which is what makes prices from several stores show together) and deletes the other. It cannot be undone.
tools.nameDuplicatesHint: Same name, different identifiers: the product was stored twice because its identifier changed later (the brand became known, the name was fixed by hand, the slug formula changed). Both show up on the site, and the abandoned record usually has no brand, no image and the price from the last collection that saw it.
tools.confirmMerge: Merge "{drop}" into "{keep}"? Offers move to a single product and the other is deleted. This cannot be undone.
tools.confirmMergeBatch: Merge {count, plural, =1 {1 selected duplicate} other {# selected duplicates}}? In each case the offers move to a single product and the other record is deleted. This cannot be undone.
tools.confirmMergeAll: Merge ALL {count} listed duplicates? In each case the offers move to a single product and the other record is deleted. This cannot be undone.
tools.mergeBatchPartial: {merged, plural, =0 {None merged} =1 {1 merged} other {# merged}}, {failed, plural, =1 {1 failed — reload the page to see which} other {# failed — reload the page to see which}}.
tools.replacementsHint: Fix product NAMES in bulk. Example: the collector strips the "Cerveja" prefix, leaving "Alemã Paulaner Münchner Hell" — a rule FROM "Alemã " (with the space) TO empty fixes them all.
tools.brandMovedHint: Brand rules are no longer created here — register the brand at /admin/marcas (canonical name + country + aliases), which is now the authority over products.brand. Old brand rules keep working until you migrate them.
tools.ruleBreakdown: {appliable, plural, =0 {none appliable now} =1 {1 appliable now} other {# appliable now}}{conflicts, plural, =0 {} =1 {, 1 is a duplicate} other {, # are duplicates}}
tools.applyRuleBlocked: Nothing to apply: every product this rule affects would end up with another product's identifier. Merge the duplicates above first.
tools.resyncResult: {count, plural, =0 {No identifier needed adjusting — the catalog is in sync with the collector.} =1 {1 identifier resynced.} other {# identifiers resynced.}} {conflicts, plural, =0 {} =1 {1 case was skipped as a duplicate — resolve it by merging.} other {# cases were skipped as duplicates — resolve them by merging.}}
tools.ignoreHint: Marks this pair as "not a duplicate" and removes it from the list for good. Nothing is deleted or merged — both products stay separate. You can undo it in the ignored section.
tools.ignoredTitle: {count, plural, =1 {1 ignored duplicate} other {# ignored duplicates}}
tools.ignoredHint: Pairs you marked as "not duplicates". They no longer show in the lists above until you bring them back here.
tools.rewriteCountriesHint: Two rules, in this order: (1) for an own store, the store's country OVERWRITES the product's — this is what fixes a store switched from marketplace to own; (2) a product with no country gets the most common country among products of the same brand. Does not change the product identifier.
tools.rewriteCountriesResult: {byStore, plural, =0 {No country rewritten from an own store} =1 {1 country rewritten from the own store} other {# countries rewritten from own stores}}. {byBrand, plural, =0 {None filled in from the brand.} =1 {1 filled in from the brand.} other {# filled in from the brand.}}
